And so that this may obtain perpetual force, we have decided to strengthen it with our hand, and have ordered it to be signed beneath with the impression of our ring. King Dagobert subscribed. Dado, referendary, presented [it]. Given at the palace of Clichy, in the eleventh year of our reign, happily in the name of God. Amen.
XIX.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives to the monastery of Saint-Denis the estate of Vallis and the estate of Argenterias (year 634).

In the name of the Lord God eternal and of our saviour Jesus Christ, Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man. If we bestow the munificence of our liberality on holy places dedicated to divine worship, we in no way doubt that this will certainly help us to pass through the present life more easily and to obtain the future one more happily. Let the diligence of all the faithful of the holy Church of God and of our own, both present and future, therefore know that for the sake of eternal reward we grant to Saint Denis, outstanding among martyrs, and to the brethren serving God there, certain estates of our right, which are situated in the district of Bourges, namely the estate called Vallis, which lies on the river Cher, and the estate called Argenterias, lying on the river Magneuria, with all their appurtenances; for which reason we have ordered this precept of our highness to be made and given to the aforesaid Saint Denis and to the brethren serving the Lord there, so that they may hold and possess the said estates perpetually without anyone's opposition. And so that this may be preserved inviolably through all times, we have confirmed this our present authority with our own hand and ordered it to be marked with our ring. S. of Dagobert, most glorious king. S. of Clovis, son of Dagobert. S. of Arnulf, bishop of Metz. Given by the hand of Dado, chancellor of the royal dignity. This was done at Paris, happily in the name of God. Amen. Given on the fourth day before the Ides of April, in the twelfth indiction, [in the] thirteenth [year] of the reign of King Dagobert.
XX.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he confers the estate of Wallare in the forest of Fagne on Landelin, with many appurtenances, for building a monastery there (year 634).

In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen. It is not fitting that it should escape the excellence of royal majesty that there is one, sole and everlasting King of kings and Lord of lords, from whom also all power is, and was, and will be for ever, to whom belongs all that we are and can be, in whom we live and move, before whom we ought to stand according to the strength he has granted us, and, the more we are exalted, the more we ought always, as far as lies in us, to increase with royal munificence and special devotion the worship and adornment of his only bride, the most holy Church. Wherefore I, Dagobert, king of the Austrasians, for the soul of Chlothar, most pious king, my father, who reigned forty-five years in Francia, induced by the persuasion and salutary counsels of the venerable man Aubert, bishop of Cambrai, grant and give to Landelin Maurosus, converted from [being] a robber, my estate in the Fagne called Wallare, with the estates, lands, forests, meadows, waters and watercourses noted below and assigned with fixed boundaries, so that he may build a monastery there in honour of the holy apostles Peter and Paul and establish persons to serve the Lord God there in perpetuity: the estate of Bavia with all its territory, the water itself and its course as it flows down through that territory, beginning at the place called Railhiez until it descends into the water of the Elpra; the whole forest called Aetimundi, with all its territory, tithe, pannage, jurisdiction and ban, from the forest of Baileporis to the aforesaid water between Bavia and Wallare; and from that same water, the whole forest which is called Brolium, and Fania, and Mansilium, and Clarus Voionus, and Wiellemanus; the forest near Wilheis, from the hill of Gomundus and Merdosus Voionus as far as the estate of Wilheis; the forest of Ducio, as the endowment of the church to be built on my aforesaid estate. Whatever within the bounds of the aforesaid forests can bring advantage or profit in any way whatever, I give by my munificence to the aforesaid Landelin to be possessed in perpetuity, with the approval of the princes and seniors of my palace, Arnulf and Pippin. And so that this our grant may obtain the force of perpetual royal firmness, I confirm the aforesaid page with my hand and decree that it be secured by the affixing of my seal. Sign of the lord Dagobert, king of the Austrasians. S. of Arnulf of Metz. S. of Pippin of Neustria, seniors of the palace. I, Anso, chancellor, in place of Cunibert the archchancellor, have checked [it]. Given at Cambrai, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the six hundred and fortieth year of the Lord's Incarnation, in the thirteenth indiction.
XXI. Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives the estate of Sarclidas to the poor matricularii of Saint-Denis (year 635).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man, to Duke Wandelbert. Whatever we confer with full devotion for feeding the poor, we trust that for this we shall have the repayment of reward in the future. Let your diligence therefore know that the estate called Sarclidas [The printed editions have Sarclitas], situated on the river Juine in the district of Étampes, which we received in exchange from the lord Ferreolus, bishop of the city of Autun, and from Deodatus the abbot, and from the clergy and the church or basilica of the lord Symphorian, where they are known to serve, for another estate named Amica, which is in the territory of Marseilles, we have, for the profit of our reward, [given], that same Sarclidas in its entirety and with its full value, to the *matricularii* [poor enrolled on the church's register] of the lord Denis the martyr, where that precious lord rests in the body, who are seen to reside at that basilica or within its forecourt on the registers; and whatever anyone may wish to add to it hereafter for their sustenance, this we have granted with full devotion. We command therefore that from the present day they possess the above-written estate of Sarclidas, with houses, slaves, vineyards, forests, meadows, pastures, mills, flocks with their shepherds, adjacent lands, and all its entirety and boundary, just as it was possessed with all firmness by the aforesaid holy church of Autun, or of the lord Symphorian, since we, as we have said, exchanged it by common agreement, another estate having been given. Therefore, since it has been granted from our generosity, for the salvation of our soul, to these matricularii of the lord Denis, without entry of judges, in perpetuity, God being favourable, let neither the abbot nor any other person whatever presume at any time to take that property away from the donation to these matricularii, but let it be administered from it in the name of God by the hand of their abbot, with whom lies the daily sustenance of these poor; and whatever the fisc could have gained from it in fines or remaining dues, let it go to these poor as an increase, so that it may please them, and those who succeed them, to pray more often for the stability of our kingdom and the salvation of our soul. And so that this precept may endure for undisturbed times, we have decided to strengthen it with our own hand. Ursinus presented [it]. King Dagobert subscribed. Given on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of August, in the fourteenth year of our reign, at Clichy, happily. Amen.
XXII.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives the estate of Aquaputa to the monastery of Saint-Denis (year 635).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man. A man, always, both when he is in good health and as if he were laid low by sickness, ought to watch more attentively over the salvation of his soul, so that he may be able to obtain a reward in the future. Therefore we, out of regard for God and for the remedy of our soul, give to the monastery of Saint Denis, where that precious lord rests in the body, and where we wish to be buried, and we wish it to be given in perpetuity, our estate which is called Aquaputa, situated in the district of Paris, with all its right and entirety. Wherefore by the present cession we decree, and we wish it to endure perpetually, the Lord protecting [it], that this estate, with all its entirety and its appurtenances, shall pass by the present authority, by most secure right, to the aforesaid monastery, and to the abbot Dodo, who is seen to preside there as ruler, so that hereafter, with lands, houses, slaves, vineyards, woods, fields, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, flocks with their shepherds, appurtenances, dependencies and any other benefits whatever, just as it has been possessed until now by our fisc, so by our indulgence, for the salvation of our soul and the stability of our sons, it may go as an increase to that holy place, and to those brothers who serve God there, in our times and in times to come. And so that this cession may be held more firmly, and be preserved unimpaired for long times with our successors, we have confirmed it below as best we could, and ordered it to be sealed with our ring. Ursinus presented [it], King Dagobert subscribed. Given on the day of the Kalends of August, in the fourteenth year of our reign, at Clichy, happily. Amen.
XXIII.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, on the foundation of the monastery of Rebais, and the immunities granted to it (year 635).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man, to our apostolic fathers the lord bishops and to the illustrious men the dukes, and likewise to the magnificent count Chanulf, and to all agents, both in present and in future times, established everywhere in the name of God in our kingdom. It befits princely clemency, among other petitions, to receive with a favourable hearing what is put forward for salvation or requested out of fear of the divine name, and without doubt to bring it to effect; so that there may be an exchange for reward when a fitting petition is granted for the quiet of the servants of God; for perfect faith does not doubt that it pertains to the grace of the Most High if anything is expended with devout mind, according to his word, especially on those of the household of faith, since it is written: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Therefore, since the illustrious man Dado, our referendary, and his brothers Ado and Rado, devoutly, with God's help, have built the monastery of Jerusalem in honour of Saint Peter and Paul and Saint Anthony, which is commonly called Rebais, situated in the territory of Meaux, for monks and pilgrims to dwell in and to enjoy the solitary life in the name of God, which they obtained also from our generosity, therefore it has pleased us, according to their petition, for the quiet of the servants of God, to publish a precept of our authority, through which, since [the monastery] is seen to have been built and in part endowed on our fisc, which we granted for the remedy of our soul, these monks may be able to dwell there perpetually under the quiet of tranquillity, the Lord protecting them, according to the norm of religion; we have chosen that this document should declare more fully that nothing of canonical authority is overturned if anything, as we have said, is granted to those of the household of faith for the tranquillity of peace; nor let anyone, disparaging us, think that we decree something new in this, since from of old, according to the constitutions of the pontiffs, by royal sanction, the monasteries of the saints of Agaune, of Lérins, of Luxeuil, and indeed also the monks of the lord Marcellus, are seen to stand under the privilege of liberty. Therefore whatever has been delegated there in estates, slaves, or any other things and livestock, whether by royal gift or by the aforesaid men or by anyone else, or shall henceforth be added, since it has been built, as we have said, on our generosity, let none of the bishops, neither the present ones nor those who shall be their successors, nor their ordainers, nor any person whatever, be able in any manner to take [anything] away from that place, or to assume any power for himself in that monastery, or to diminish anything as if under the title of exchange, or to remove anything from the ornaments of the sacred rites or from the offering brought to the altar; nor let even a bishop presume to come to that monastery or its cells, except to gain [the fruit of] prayer, unless it be with the will of the abbot himself or of his congregation, [and] without heavy expense to them, so that the monks of that place, living by the rule in the name of God, may the more easily possess the rightful delegation in quiet through the ages; and when that abbot has been called from the world, whomever the congregation itself chooses from among themselves, let it install him as senior according to the holy rule in all things and from all, supported according to the wish of the delegation and the text of this authority, so that for him all things there may go to increase without any disturbance. We add that no judge whatever, nor any man, shall have licence to defraud anything of the property of the aforesaid monastery without the will of the servants of God, or with rash spirit to (assign) anything from it to his own uses, lest, which is first, he incur the divine and our displeasure..... (So in the editions) sustain heavy damage from the fisc..... (So in the editions) and further it has pleased us, weighing the merits for our full reward and that of the aforesaid men, to add that, both on the possessions which from our generosity and those which from the delegation of Dado himself and his brothers, or of their parents, or of anyone whatever, have been or shall be conveyed there at any time, no public judicial power, neither present nor succeeding, shall presume to enter there to hear cases or to exact anything; but under full immunity this monastery and its congregation shall possess for themselves all the fines granted, and whatever the fisc might perhaps have been able to expect from it, from their men, whether free or serving, or dwelling on their lands, or from whatever source, all of it by our indulgence shall go, for the gain of reward, to the lights of that holy place and the stipends of the servants of God, both while we live in the name of God and in succeeding times, so that it may please these monks to implore continually the immense mercy of God for eternal salvation and perpetual happiness and the constancy of the kingdom. That this precept of our decree, Christ assisting in all things, may be held more firmly, we have taken care to have the subscription of our hand written below. King Dagobert subscribed. Dado presented [it]. Given on the day of the Kalends of October, [in the] fourteenth [year] of his reign.
XXIV.

Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives to the monks of Saint-Denis the estates of Tauriacum, Tibernio, Rubridum, Monarvilla and Vasconis Vallis (year 635). Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man. It ought to be desirable, while we remain in this transitory life, to raise up the places of the saints [Royal cartulary: the place] from transitory things for eternal reward, for the nourishment and support of the servants of God, so that from transitory things we may earn eternal ones. Therefore we, considering this, give estates of our right, that is, Tauriacum, Tibernio and Rubridum, situated in the district of Orléans, and also Monarvilla [and Monarvilla is lacking in the royal cartulary], and Vasconis Vallis in the district of Étampes, to the brother monks serving at the basilica of the lord Denis, our special patron, where the abbot Aigulf is seen to preside, and where we wish to be buried, to be administered in perpetuity specially for their nourishment. These aforesaid estates, with all jurisdictions and lordships [these three words are lacking in the cartulary], lands, houses, slaves, vineyards, woods, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, and all appurtenances, we grant by our munificence, by special donation, for nourishment to the aforesaid holy place and the monks serving God there, so that they, making use of the aforesaid estates, may entreat God with daily prayer for us and our offspring, that he may protect us by his mercy, for love of whom we have conferred these things on them. And so that this donation of our authority may obtain inviolable firmness through succeeding times, we have decided to strengthen it below with the subscription of our hand [and] the impression of our ring. King Dagobert subscribed. Dado presented [it]. Given in the month of October, in the eighth year of our reign, in the name of God, at the palace of Clichy, happily. Amen.
XXV.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives Molliacum to the monks of Saint-Denis (year 635).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man. It ought to be our wish, while we remain in this perishable life, to relieve the places of the saints out of transitory goods for an eternal reward, for the nourishment and support of the servants of God, so that by perishable goods we may earn eternal ones. Therefore, considering these things, we give an estate of our right which is called Malliacus, situated in the district of Bourges, two miles distant from the river Cher, to the brother monks serving at the basilica of the lord Denis the martyr, our special patron, where the abbot Aigulf is seen to preside, and where we wish to be buried, to be administered in perpetuity specially for their nourishment. Therefore the aforesaid estate, with lands, lordships, slaves, male and female serfs, woods, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, and all appurtenances, we grant by our munificence, by special donation, for nourishment to the aforesaid holy place and the monks serving there, so that they, making use of the goods from the aforesaid estate, may entreat God with daily prayer for us and our offspring, that he may protect us by his mercy, for love of whom we have conferred these things on them. And so that this donation of our authority may inviolably obtain firmness through succeeding times, we have decided to strengthen it below with the subscription of our hand. King Dagobert subscribed. Dado the chancellor presented [it]. Sign of Arnulf, bishop of Metz. S[ign] of Eligius, bishop of Noyon. S[ign] of Aigulf, abbot of the monastery of the lord Denis. Given in the month of October, in the fourteenth year of our reign. Done, in the name of God, at the palace of Clichy, happily, amen.
XXVI. Fragment of the testament of Dagobert I, king of the Franks (year 635).

In the name of the Trinity of the Lord God almighty. To the apostolic Fathers, that is, the bishops and abbots, and the other priests dwelling in our kingdom, Dagobert, king of the Franks. As far as the understanding of human sense can weigh with a shrewd mind and consider with careful inquiry, nothing is of more value for gaining, in the light of this world and its fleeting joys, than that one should be eager to spend out of transitory goods on venerable places for the nourishment of the poor; so that those who in common suffer the frailty of nature may keep watch for the salvation of the soul before a sudden removal comes, so that no one may be found unprepared, or depart from the world without any regard [for it]. Rather, while he still stands in the right of his own freedom, let him be eager to purchase out of perishable substance perpetual life in the eternal tabernacles, so that he may be able to attain a desirable place in the fellowship of the just, etc. [And likewise, after a little:] Accordingly it has pleased us, with sound mind and sound counsel, and, as we have said, divine devotion has admonished us, that for our salvation and for eternal recompense we should order a testament to be written, and for an unchangeable benefit we have confirmed four [copies] in one tenor, and whatever we have conferred anywhere on the places of the saints we have woven into it with like record: of these we have sent one to Lyon in Gaul, and another we have entrusted to the archives of the church at Paris. [As was said above. Then it is added:] We give therefore to the basilica of the lord Vincent at Paris, where we intend to have [our] burial whenever God shall order it, and we decree that it be given in perpetuity, the estate called Cumbis villa, in the district of Paris, which Ursa, daughter of Aldericus, held. In like manner to the basilica of the blessed Peter the apostle at Paris, where Saint Genevieve rests in the body, the estate of Dravernum in Brie. (And to the basilica of the lord Denis, likewise at Paris, where he rests with his companions, the estate of Braunate in Brie.) To the basilica of the lady Columba, and of the lord Lupus at Sens, the estate of Grande Campum in the Gâtinais, etc. [Many more things are contained there. And at the end he added:] But you, good sons, considering first the bond of nature, by whose grace it binds even beasts, remain brothers; do not cast off that with which you are laden. Then revere me your Father, who prefer to ask though I could command, that you keep our statutes unshaken, just as you would wish yours to be kept by your successors, knowing for certain that if you hold in contempt what has been sanctioned by us, which I do not think [you will], in like manner your decrees too will be held in contempt by those after you.
XXVII.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he confers very many gifts in the border region of Limoges and Bourges on the monastery of Saint-Denis (year 636).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man. Since it is shown by certain and daily signs to be true that the matter and condition of all who are born returns to nothing in a moment of time, the salvation of our souls demands that each one, whom the negligence of the first man makes an exile and a stranger, should daily examine the manner of his whole life, and then, while the last lot has not yet snatched away the breath of life, should exert himself to obtain by his merits a place there whence he first fell, and where after his passing his soul is to return under angelic guidance. Therefore I, Dagobert, king of the Franks, crowned by God, whom by permission of the highest King and by grant of our predecessors Francia obeys and serves, now treating of the salvation of my soul and using sounder counsel, have resolved with myself to make one of the soldiers of Christ my helper and neighbour by the donation of certain of my possessions. This is, namely, the renowned and precious witness Denis, who once, stripped of fear, girded with the fervour of faith, came to Gaul, and there, while the faithlessness of the heathen was spreading, manfully resisted, constant in faith, preaching and disclosing the teaching of the holy law. For since by the shedding of his own blood he is known to sit at the right hand of God, and continually to obtain [grace] for those for whom he wishes to ask, the whole world ought to venerate him with the highest service: much indeed I [ought], who in escaping my father's anger felt that his grace was not absent from me. Wherefore, although the aforesaid Denis needs nothing for the glory which he happily enjoys with God, yet so that he may become for me, with my own wife and children, a most faithful intercessor before the just Judge, and also the excuser of our faults on the day of judgement, [therefore] for the monks of that monastery in which sinners with groans approach him resting in the body and confess their sins, and where the abbot Leobafarius is seen to preside, we decree that certain possessions situated in the border region of Limousin and Bourges, hitherto assigned to the royal domain, are to be held in quiet through the courses of succeeding times. Their names, so that they may be plain to all, we recite, listing them below as follows: first, namely, our fortress which is called Patriagus, with the churches and also the estates belonging to that fortress, and with the churches, and also everything which is known hitherto to have been under its lordship, we transfer from this day onward into the right and lordship of the brothers of the monastery of the same martyr of Christ, Denis. Next, our estate which is called Patriacus, situated on the river Jugia, with our chapel consecrated in honour of the Holy Saviour, and with the three churches existing in the same estate, and with all its appurtenances. We add moreover two other estates, with churches, which are situated on the river Vulsia, namely Petra Ficta and Patriacum with the demesne meadow, and with all their appurtenances, and our estate which is called Fornolis, with male and female serfs, and Nigromons with [its] church, and Campaniacum with [its] church. We give also the cell of Larundum and the parish church, with all the churches belonging to that fortress, both within and without. Adding also in the district of Bourges, we grant the estate of Casimansus with [its] church, the estate of Lanatidum with [its] church, the estate of Giuretae with [its] church, the estate of Archiniacum with [its] church, the estate of Maniacum with [its] church, the estate of Stivaliculae with [its] church, and five manses belonging to the same church, the estate of Guierlaicum with [its] church, the estate of Vernidum with [its] church, the estate of Duae Casae with [its] church, the estate of Vicus Plenus with [its] church, the estate of Perolium with [its] church and demesne field, the estate of Vallum with [its] church, the estate of Argenteria with [its] church, the estate of Notum with [its] church, the estate of Umreziacum with [its] church, the estate of Napsiniacum with [its] church; and whatever is seen to belong to these estates, with male and female serfs, lands, meadows, woods, mills, waters and watercourses. We give besides all the land which lies between two waters, from the river Conus as far as the stream of the spring of Maer, with all the churches: namely the church of Saint Martial of Salviacum, and the church of Cursiacum, the church of Mosaycum, and also all the possessions belonging to these churches, both within and without, up to the place where these two waters join, besides our chapel consecrated in honour of the blessed Martin, with two estates belonging to that church, namely Golaocum, and the other which is called Longavilla, which the lord Godinus, apostolic man, archbishop of Lyon, held from the royal majesty. See what I offer to the blessed Denis and to those who serve him. If by chance anyone of those succeeding us on the throne of the kingdom, which God forbid, or any very powerful person, inflicting losses on them, brings these back into his own lordship, then, just as I hope to be saved by his intercession in giving them, so may that invader, in retaining them, be condemned to the worst death. And so that this gift may not seem spurious to those after us, but stable, and so that this charter may be firmer through the ages, we have ordained that it be strengthened and confirmed by the sign of our hand. Sign of Dagobert, illustrious king. Sign of Archbishop Palladius. Sign of Bishop Landericus. Sign of Bishop Laudomerus. Sign of Bishop Fraudobertus. Sign of Bishop Asterius. Sign of Bishop Eligius. Sign of Bishop Franemundus. Sign of Bishop Sylvinus. Sign of Bishop Lauradus. S[ign] of Bishop Maurinus. S. of Bishop Clarus. S. of Bishop Gradonus. S. of Bishop John. S. of Abbot Burgundofaro. S. of Leobafarius, abbot of Saint-Denis. S. of the prefect Mummolus. S. of Count Gundoenus. S. of Count Chariullus. S. of Count Audinus. S. of Count Dructoaldus. S. of Count Charimundus. Dado, archbishop of the Church of Rouen, consenting, subscribed. Given on the third day before the Kalends of August, in the fifteenth year of our reign. Done at the palace of Compiègne, happily. Amen.
XXVIII.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives the estates of Noth and Pascellarius to the monks of Saint-Denis (year 636).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man. Before a man dies by sudden death, he ought to keep watch for the salvation of his soul, lest perhaps death, taking away the present light without any regard, should find someone unprepared, and so hand him over to perpetual darkness and eternal torments. Therefore, while he still stands in the right of his own freedom, he ought to seek to purchase out of perishable possessions everlasting life in the eternal dwellings. For this reason I, for the relief of my soul, grant to the monks of the basilica of the lord Denis, our special patron, in which that precious martyr rests in the body with his companions, and where we wish to be buried, and where Abbot Aigulf is also known to preside, the estate called Noth, and another which is called Pascellarius, with their appurtenances, situated in the district of Bourges, and the slaves of both sexes, with meadows, fields, woods, waters and watercourses, just as they have hitherto been possessed by our fisc; so, by our indulgence, for the gaining of the salvation of our soul and for the stability of our sons, may they benefit from and hold [them] in present and future time for ever; and let none of our sons, or of the kings of the Franks our successors, nor bishop, nor abbot of that monastery, nor any powerful person presume to take away the aforesaid estates, which we have granted to that holy place, if he does not wish to incur the wrath of God and the displeasure of the lord Denis. And so that this precept may be held firmer and preserved through the ages, and may have firmer force, we have decreed that it be strengthened below by the subscriptions of our hand. Sign of King Dagobert. Sign of his son Clovis. Sign of Eligius, his goldsmith. Sign of Dado, his chancellor. Sign of Abbot Geremarus. Sign of Abbot Aigulf. Given on the day of the Kalends of November, in the fifteenth year of our reign. Done at the palace of Clichy, happily. Amen.
XXIX.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he grants the estate of Iticinascoa to the church of Saint-Denis (year 637).

[Dago]bert, king of the Franks, to the illustrious men Duke Vandelbert, the *domesticus* [household officer] Raganricus, and all agents present and future... [space of eight syllables left blank] eternal, and from perishable substance to be paid out to earn everlasting joys. Therefore we, considering this very thing, so that we may deserve for eternity even a little the fellowship of the just, the estate... [space of three syllables] named Iticinascoa, in the district of Paris, which belonged to Landericus and [space of one letter] his brothers, with its additions... [space of four syllables] or merit, to the basilica of the lord Denis, martyr, our special patron, where that precious lord is known to rest in the body... we are devoted through the ages, with the Lord's favour, to bestow goods, we are seen to have granted in person with full devotion. Commanding indeed... [with fields,] woods, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, from the present day, as by them... is held, or is possessed by our fisc at the present time in the name of God, granted by our indulgence to that holy basilica, which... from [our] authority they may receive more especially... for the poor dwelling there, for the stability of the kingdom or the relief of our soul, without any later opposition in times to come it ought to benefit, and so that it may happen that while we for the clergy or the poor and that holy place standing... or in any little way... any... inconvenience be produced. And so that... [space of four syllables. Mabillon partly supplies thus: And so that... through the ages inviolable, etc.] it may take inviolable firmness, [with the subscriptions of our] hand below... King Dagobert subscribed. Dado presented [it]. [Place of the seal.] on the fifteenth day, in the tenth year of our reign, in God's [name]... at Clichy, happily.
XXX.

Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he grants to Bishop Amand a place between the rivers Elnone and Scarpe, suitable for those serving as soldiers of God to be established there (year 637).

In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Dagobert, by the ordinance of divine clemency, king. We believe that God will be propitious to us if we devote special care to reforming and confirming the practice of religion, and open the hand of our munificence and liberality to those who serve religion. Accordingly, we wish the diligence of those present and to come to know that Amand, a bishop of venerable life, who by the grace of God baptised our son Sigebert, having already built and well ordered certain churches and monasteries for the increase of divine worship, approached our excellence and, as an unfailing cultivator of the Lord's vineyard, trusting moreover in the benefit of our generosity, humbly asked that a place situated between two rivers, the Scarpe and the Elnone, be granted to him by our liberality: this place, although because of the great density of the forest it was difficult to clear, nevertheless seemed suitable for his labour, or rather, after his labour, for the rest and use of those serving as soldiers of God, whom he was already piously planning, by the grace of God, to establish there. We therefore, considering the worthy petition of the reverend bishop, both for the stability and peace of our whole kingdom and of our offspring, and for the salvation of our souls, have granted with ready devotion of mind the place he had asked for, with both waters and the forest growing all around, and we establish the grant by the ratified sanction of the laws. We therefore command, and by royal authority order, that no secular or ecclesiastical person attempt to cause the bishop himself or his successors any disturbance or opposition, or prejudice or violence, concerning the aforesaid place, with the water and forest, granted to the aforesaid bishop by our liberality; but rather that both the bishop himself and those whom he establishes there, and those who succeed him, hold and possess this benefit of royal munificence securely and in perpetuity, without any diminution, without any false claim or contradiction. And if divine goodness should wish the place to be improved and enlarged through the industry of this lovable man and his successors, and through the devout generosity of good men, whatever the right of the fisc could demand from it, whether in cases, or in *freda* [fines], or in meadows, or in divisions of lands and dues, or in any other way, we grant it in full both to the aforesaid father and to his successors. And we wish that place itself and the property pertaining to it, and whatever the generosity of princes or the devotion of any of the faithful shall add hereafter, to stand under the defence of our protection and immunity. And so that this royal authority may continue firm and unshaken for ever, we confirm the present precept below with our own hand, and seal it with the impression of our ring. We also urge our successors to imitate our practice in this very matter. Given on the Kalends of May, in the seventh indiction, in the eleventh year of the reign of the lord Dagobert. Done at the city of Paris, happily. Amen.
XXXI.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he grants the monastery of Saint-Denis immunity from every power (year 637).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man, to Mummolus the prefect, to Gondoenus, Werpenus, Dructoaldus, Audinus, Charimundus and Chariulfus, counts, and to all agents, present and future. It befits princely clemency, among other petitions, to receive with a favourable hearing that which is put forward for salvation and requested in the divine name, and without doubt to bring it to effect, so that eternal things may be gained from the perishable things of the present age, according to the precept of the Lord who says: Make yourselves friends of the mammon of iniquity. Therefore, according to his saying, we ought to purchase eternal and heavenly things with the mammon of iniquity, so that while we bestow fitting benefits on the priests of Christ, we may earn by this to have the Lord as rewarder in the eternal dwellings. Accordingly, the venerable Aigulf, abbot of the basilica of our special patron the lord Denis, martyr, where that precious lord rests in the body, petitioned the clemency of our reign that, in accordance with what we dealt with some days ago at Compiègne in our general court, we would now likewise, by our own authority, under the immunity of our name, anew for the firmness of the matter, deign in God's name to grant and confirm this concerning that holy place and the men who might wish to hand over and devote themselves, with their substance and property, to that holy basilica. Therefore let your greatness and diligence know that we, out of reverence for those saints and for the quiet of the monks serving God there, have with most ready will granted this anew, and let your diligence see that we have confirmed it in all respects. Wherefore, by this precept which we decree more especially and wish to endure for ever, we order and establish that neither you, your subordinates, nor your successors in perpetuity, nor anyone invested with judicial power, shall presume at any time to enter or make demands within the immunity of Saint-Denis, upon the estates of the aforesaid basilica of the lord Denis, wherever they may be, in whatever regions or districts in our kingdom by God's favour, which the side of that monastery is known to possess and hold at the present day, or which has been granted there by God-fearing men through lawful charters, or shall hereafter be added or assigned, neither to hear cases, nor to take sureties, nor to exact *freda* or bans, nor to make lodgings or provisions, nor to demand any dues; but whatever our fisc could exact from it, all and from all, we grant from the present day, for the increase of our reward, under full and most firm immunity; and if anyone wishes to break this our authority or immunity, and leads others to do so, let each of them for himself be compelled to pay thirty pounds of the purest gold in compensation to the side of Saint-Denis; and, as has been said, whatever our fisc might perhaps have expected from it for our part, let it be granted and conceded in full in perpetuity by our decrees for the lights or the stipends of the monks, and the sustenance of the poor of that monastery, so that it may please them the better to pray more earnestly for the mercy of the Lord for the stability of our kingdom, for its quiet, and for all our leudes. So that this authority may remain perpetually firm and inviolate concerning that holy place in our times and in times to come, may be kept and preserved unharmed through all ages, and so that you may believe it better and more surely, along with all our magnates and public and private judges, we have decreed that it be strengthened below by the subscriptions of our hand, and have ordered it to be sealed with our ring. King Dagobert subscribed. Dado presented [it]. Given on the fourth day before the Kalends of August, in the second year of our reign. At Compiègne, in God's name, happily. Amen.
XXXII.
Another diploma on the same subject, with additions (year 637).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man, to all bishops, abbots, dukes, counts, centenarii and our other agents, both present and future. Among other petitions, it befits princely clemency to receive with a favourable hearing what is set down for the salvation of the soul and asked in the divine name, and without doubt to bring it to effect, so that by means of the perishable things of the present the eternal life to follow may be gained, according to the precept of the Lord, who says: Make yourselves friends of the mammon of iniquity. Therefore, according to his own saying, we ought to purchase eternal and heavenly things with the mammon of iniquity, so that, while we bestow fitting benefits on the church of Christ, we may deserve to have the Lord as our rewarder for this in the eternal tabernacles. So the venerable Aigulf, abbot of the basilica of our special patron the lord Denis the martyr, where that precious lord rests in the body, has petitioned the clemency of our reign that, in accordance with what we dealt with some days ago at Compiègne in our general court, so now (in our universal synod assembled at Paris), by our own authority, under the name of immunity, we would deign once again, for the firmness of the matter, to grant and confirm this in God's name concerning that holy place, and the men who have wished to hand over and devote themselves, with their substance or property, to that holy basilica. Therefore let your greatness and diligence know that, out of reverence for those saints and for the quiet of the monks serving God there, we have with most ready will granted this once again and confirmed it in all respects. Wherefore by this precept, which we decree in particular and wish to endure in perpetuity, we order and establish that neither we nor our successors, nor anyone, nor an archbishop, (nor anyone whatever) girded with judicial power, shall ever have any power (over that holy basilica or those dwelling in it, except by the will of the abbot and his monks; but let this holy mother church, namely that of our special patron the lord and great Denis, be free and quit of all invasion or disturbance from all men, of whatever order or power they may be). Into the estates of the aforesaid basilica of the lord Denis, wherever they are, in whatever regions or districts within our kingdom, God being gracious, which the side of that monastery is seen to possess and hold from the present day, or which has been granted to it by God-fearing men through lawful charter instruments, or shall hereafter be added or assigned, let no one presume at any time to enter or make demands within the immunity of Saint-Denis, whether to hear cases, or to take sureties, or to exact freda [peace-money] or bans, or to claim lodgings or provisions, or to require any dues; but whatever our fisc could have exacted from them, all of it and from all of them, for the increase of our reward, we grant from the present day under full and most firm immunity (to that holy place, and we confirm it in perpetuity). But if anyone should wish to infringe this our authority or immunity, and should draw others into it, let each of them for himself pay thirty pounds of the purest gold in compensation to the side of Saint-Denis; and, as has been said, whatever our fisc might have expected from it for our part, let it be granted and conceded in full in perpetuity by our decrees for the lights or the stipends of the monks, and for the alms of the poor of that monastery, so that it may please them the better to pray more earnestly for the mercy of the Lord for the stability of our kingdom, for its quiet, and for all our leudes. And so that this authority may remain perpetually firm and inviolate concerning that holy place in our times and in times to come, and may be kept and preserved unharmed through all ages, and may be believed better and more surely by all our magnates and public and private judges, we have decreed that it be strengthened below by the subscriptions of our hand, and have ordered it to be sealed with our ring. King Dagobert subscribed. (Bishop Palladius subscribed. Bishop Taurinus subscribed. Bishop Eligius subscribed. Bishop Silvinus subscribed. Bishop Orado subscribed. Bishop Clarus subscribed. Count Gondoenus subscribed. I, Dado, presented [it]. Bishop Johannes subscribed. Bishop Richoaldus subscribed. Bishop Atherius subscribed. Bishop Laudomerus subscribed. Bishop Landericus subscribed. Bishop Acterius subscribed. Mummolus, prefect, subscribed.) Given on the fourth day before the Kalends of August, in the tenth year of our reign, at Paris, in God's name, happily, amen.
XXXIII.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he confers Reuilly and many other gifts on the monastery of Saint-Denis (year 637).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man. Since it is shown by sure and daily signs to be true that the substance and condition of all who are born returns to nothing in a moment of time, the salvation of our souls demands that each person, whom the negligence of the first man makes an exile and a pilgrim, should examine daily the manner of his whole life, and then, before the final lot has snatched away his living breath, should strive to obtain through his merits a place there whence he first fell, and where after his passing his soul is to return under the guidance of angels. For who, setting out for any city, perhaps for the sake of trade or driven by necessity, does not send ahead some goods with which he may be well content and have enough, all want removed? And so, since it is clear that the Apostle said: While we have time, let us do good to all, it is to be committed to memory by each of the orthodox, who confesses himself the creature and temple of Christ, that, while the law and rights of the death that is owed still allow him the span of living, he should give out and bestow his goods for Christ; and thus, laying up treasure in the heavenly Jerusalem, he will possess a free dwelling when he returns to it, and hunger and thirst will be denied to his spirit forever. And since it is in no way to my advantage to be shut out from its bridal chamber, I, Dagobert, king of the Franks, crowned by God, whom Francia obeys and serves by the permission of the highest King and also by the grant of our predecessors, now treating of the salvation of my soul and following sounder counsel, have resolved within myself to make one of the soldiers of Christ my helper and neighbour by the gift of certain of my properties. This is the renowned and precious witness Denis, who once, stripped of fear and girded with the fervour of faith, came to Gaul, and there, while the faithlessness of the heathen was sprouting, resisted manfully, constant in faith, preaching and revealing the doctrine of the holy law. Him, who through the shedding of his own blood is known to sit at the right hand of God and to obtain continually for those for whom he wishes to ask, the whole world ought to venerate with the highest devotion; and I above all, who, in escaping my father's anger, felt his grace to be present with me. Wherefore, although the aforesaid Denis needs nothing, given the glory he happily enjoys with God, yet so that he may become for me, with my own wife and children, a most faithful intercessor before the just Judge, and also the pleader for our faults on the day of judgement, we decree that the cenobites of that monastery, in which sinners approach him resting in the body with groans and confess their sins, and over which Abbot Leobafarius is seen to preside, shall hold quietly through the course of succeeding times certain properties situated in the territory of Bourges, hitherto assigned to our lordship. And so that their names may be clear and certain to all, we list them below as follows: first, Reuilly; and then these villages, namely: the estate of Fracillo, Montelliacum, Avendelliacum, Noziocum, Morilliacum, Talaicum, Sarmasiacum, Paredum, Ger, Pay, Masnile, Cassinoilum, Cantalupum, Jernacum, Vineolas, the land of Planis, the land of Valle, to which Arnolliacus belongs, the land called Mons-Beraldi, the land called Canehuces, with all their appurtenances, namely woods and vineyards, meadows, waters and their courses, and male and female slaves. Besides these, I grant [them] to have the demesne estate, with the chapel built there in honour of the Holy Saviour and his apostles Peter and Paul, and of the holy martyrs Denis, Rusticus and Eleutherius, with the enclosed vineyard, and seven mills, ten ovens, and the port, the market, and also the fisheries which I ordered to be established there for myself. I also give two estates, one of which is called Cirsai and lies on the river Theols, and the other Goyse, which is next to the river Arnon, with all their appurtenances. Behold what I offer to blessed Denis and to those who serve him. If anyone of those who succeed us on the throne of the kingdom, or any very powerful person, should perhaps (may it not happen) bring these into his own lordship, inflicting losses on him, then just as I, by giving them, hope to be saved through his intercession, so may that invader, by keeping them, be condemned to the worst death. And so that this gift may not seem spurious to posterity but stable, and so that this charter may be firmer through the ages, we have resolved that it be strengthened and confirmed by the sign of our hand. Sign of Dagobert, most glorious king; sign of Clovis his son; sign of Eligius his goldsmith; sign of Dado his chancellor; sign of Geremarus; sign of Abbot Leobafarius. Given on the day of the Kalends of September, in the twenty-fifth year of our reign. Done at the city of Orléans, happily, in God's name. Amen.
XXXIV.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives the estates of Acuciacum, Cosdunum and several others to the matricularii of the church of Saint-Denis (year 637).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man. A man, always, both when unharmed and also as if placed in sickness, ought to keep watch more attentively for the salvation of his soul, so that he may be able to acquire the gains of rewards in the future. Therefore we, out of regard for God and for the remedy of our soul, [grant] the estates named Acuciacum and Cosdunum, situated in the district of Beauvais, and moreover the estate of Magninus and the hamlet of Medianus [Dub., Magnovillare, Mediovillare], and Gellis and Averciacum, to the matricularii of the lord Denis, our special patron, where the lord himself rests in the body and where we desire to be buried, for their sustenance [Dub., we have granted for the sustenance] and maintenance: [namely that] the above-written estates of Acuciacum and Cosdunum, the estate of Magninus, the hamlet of Medianus [Dub., Magnovillare, Mediovillare], and Gellis and Averciacum, with all their appurtenance and boundary, should pass at once to these matricularii, so that hereafter, with lands, houses, slaves, vineyards, woods, meadows, pastures, flocks with their shepherds, adjacent properties and any other benefits whatsoever, just as they have until now been possessed by our fisc, so by our indulgence, for gaining the salvation of our soul and for the stability of our sons, they may benefit these matricularii, who dwell at the aforesaid holy basilica or within its forecourt, in present and future time for ever; and we have ordered this assignment to be made, being already gravely ill, and let none of our sons, or anyone else, have occasion on this account, as if attempting to oppose or resist our present will; and also let neither bishop nor abbot dare to take this away from these brethren, if he does not wish to incur the wrath of God or the displeasure of the lord Denis. But if anyone should try to overturn this, which we have ordered to be done with the Lord God himself as witness [Dub., which, with the Lord God himself as witness, we have ordered], let him render account for it before the tribunal of Christ together with these brethren; and since we are not able to provide from the hospice out of these estates, or Saclitas [Dub., Sarditas], which was previously assigned by us to these brethren, in accordance with which they receive their food for the rest from the account of the basilica, if the account is balanced, an annual living from this will, God granting, be fully able to suffice for them, so that our alms may always feed both these matricularii and their successors for our soul, whereby it may the more delight them always to pray for us; and since we have been quite unable to subscribe this precept, because the pen trembled in our hand, we have therefore asked that our sweetest son King Clovis should confirm this charter by the sign of his name, and that Dado should present it, and that our nobles should subscribe it. Sign of the glorious lord King Clovis. I, Dado [Dub., I Dado], at the command of the aforesaid lord King Dagobert, being present, have confirmed and presented the precept. Sign of the illustrious man Waldebert the seneschal, which Ragnegisel [signed] [Dub., seneschal: sign of Ragnegisel]. Sign of Frannegisel. Sign of the illustrious man Austrapius the chamberlain. Given on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of October, in the sixteenth year of our reign, at Clichy, in God's name, happily. Amen. [Dubl. adds: I, Ermenulf, wrote this.]
XXXV.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives the estate of Esterpiniacum to the basilica of Saint-Denis (year 637).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man, to all agents [Dub., our agents], present and future. It must be desirable to earn eternal things from transitory ones, and by giving out perishable substance to gain everlasting joys. Therefore we, considering this matter, so that for eternity, or in some small measure, we may merit to be companions of the just, are seen to have granted the estate whose name is Stirpiniacum [Dub., Esterpiniacum], situated in the district of the Vexin, with all its entirety and appurtenance, to the basilica of the lord Denis the martyr, our special patron, where that precious lord rests in the body and where the venerable man Abbot Aigulf is seen to preside as custodian, for the reason that we, most devoted there (Dub. lacks the word 'there') through good times, by the Lord's favour, [wished] to bestow [it] at once with full devotion; commanding indeed [Dub., and commanding we specially ordain] that the aforesaid estate, with all its entirety and soundness, that is, with houses, buildings, defences, slaves, coloni, tenants, settlers, freedmen, serfs both born there and brought from elsewhere, rural and urban, woodland pastures and adjoining lands, cultivated and uncultivated, vineyards, woods, meadows, pastures, waters and watercourses, cattle, livestock, movable and immovable [property], every kind of beast and all appurtenances in general [Dub., all appurtenances], dependencies, adjacent properties, both within the boundaries and outside the boundaries, and every property acquired, whatever can be said or named, or whatever is possessed by our fisc at the present time in God's name, be granted by our indulgence to that holy basilica: we specially ordain that hereafter it may please [it] to benefit that holy place, and the clergy and the poor dwelling there, for the stability of the kingdom and the remedy of our soul, without anyone's opposition hereafter, in his times, so that it may come about that, while we assign substance, or some small portion, to the clergy and poor dwelling at that holy place, [we may have] reward in the future with the Lord through the intercession of the aforesaid lord Denis the martyr, for what is done. And so that this grant of our authority may obtain inviolable firmness through the times both of those present and of those to come, we have resolved to mark it, as we have said, with the subscription of our hand and our own annotation. The illustrious man Dagobert subscribed. Given on the day of the Kalends of October, in the fifth year of the reign, at Sauriciagore.
XXXVI.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives the estate of Giuretis to the monastery of Saint-Denis (year 637).

Dagobert, by the grace of God king of the Franks. Before the dissolution of our life overtakes us, and as long as, by the law of the first parent, a pilgrim's dwelling here is granted to us, since it is profitable and wholesome for our souls, we ought to enlarge the holy churches of God with a bounty of present goods, which no one possesses permanently, but [they pass] with the passing of time, so that thus our immortal spirit, when it has put off the mortal man, may rejoice to obtain happy and unfading glory [Dub., may exult to obtain glory]. Wherefore I, so that, when bodily aids have failed me, I may deserve to be placed in everlasting rest, [with] my sons and also my wife, grant to the monks of the monastery of our patron Saint Denis, in which his body rests and where we desire to be laid in the tomb at the end of our burial, where Abbot Astulf [Dub., Abbot Aigulf] is seen to preside, the estate called Gyuretis [Dub., de Giurettis], with its dependencies, to be held by perpetual right; it is situated in the district of Bourges and is two miles distant from the river Cher. And if any very powerful person [Dub., anyone], by ravaging the estate, should inflict losses on the precious martyr Denis, or if any of the kings succeeding us on the throne of the kingdom should choose to recall it into his own lordship, let him suffer the wrath of God and of the martyr whose church we enrich by giving. And so that this gift may be much the firmer, and may not seem spurious to posterity in times to come, and this charter may obtain firmer force, we have decreed that it be strengthened and confirmed by the sign of our hand.

Sign of King Dagobert. Sign of Clovis [Dub., Chloudouvius] his son. Sign of Eligius his goldsmith. Sign of Dado his chancellor. Sign of Geremarus [Dub., Abbot Geremarus]. Sign of Abbot Aistulf [Dub., Aigulf].
Given on the day of the Kalends of December [Dub., September], in the thirtieth year of our reign. Done at the estate of Épinay, happily, in God's name, amen.
XXXVII.

Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he orders that the children of the slaves or serfs of the monastery of Saint-Denis be subjected in perpetuity, with their offspring, to bondage under the law of ecclesiastical slaves (year 637).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man, to all bishops, abbots, counts, dukes, vicars, centenarii, agents [Dub., actors], judges, and all who exercise authority in the whole kingdom of the Franks. If we decide by royal judgement those things which are seen to pertain to the reverence of God's holy places and to the testament of the slaves belonging to them, we seem indeed to act justly, and we therefore hope without doubt to have the reward of eternal recompense with God. Wherefore let the discernment of those present and to come know that, at the petition of the lord Chunald, venerable abbot, and of the brother monks of the monastery of the holy and most blessed lord Denis the martyr, our special patron, where the lord himself rests in the body together with his illustrious companions the martyrs Rusticus and Eleutherius, concerning the unions of slaves, serfs and maidservants both of these holy venerable martyrs and of all other men universally dwelling in the whole kingdom entrusted to us by God, whether they be ours or those of any men of whatever dignity, order and power, establishing this by this precept of our dignity, we decree that from now on, for all future times of the present age, whoever of the slaves, whether serfs or maidservants, of the aforesaid martyrs, whether male or female, by whatever arrangement, whether by lawful or clandestine union, has begotten, borne and propagated offspring, shall from then and always, without any sharer or divider, irrefutably be recalled with all their offspring into the power of the aforesaid holy martyrs and be subjected to the law [Dub., and to the law] of ecclesiastical slaves, and be bound in perpetuity under the dominion of the aforesaid abbot and of his successors, the monks serving God in the said monastery. But if anyone should presume against this decree of my majesty, and should infringe and in any way violate what we decree out of love of justice, let him, constrained by the laws, be compelled to pay ten pounds of the purest gold and twenty pounds of the most tested silver, by the weight of our palace, and be held [liable] for those slaves, if he is free; but if he is a serf, let him pay the same and be struck with a hundred and fifty blows in public before the judges. And so that this decree of our precept may remain unshaken and, receiving fuller force, be preserved inviolably through future times, we have ordered it to be marked with the ring of our dignity. Given in the tenth year of the reign of our lord [our is lacking in Dub.] Dagobert, most glorious king of the Franks. Dado, chancellor of the royal dignity, verified [it], read and reread [it] [Dub., read and reread].
XXXVIII.

Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which is confirmed the precarial charter of Sigrannus, abbot of Anille, and of Hadoindus, bishop of Le Mans, concerning the monastery of Anille (year 637).

Dagobert, king of the Franks, illustrious man. If we willingly grant, or bring to effect, those things which pertain to the needs of churches or of priests, we trust that we shall have the Lord as rewarder for it, and we trust that it pertains, in God's name, to our reward and to the stability of our kingdom. Therefore let it be known to all our faithful, present and future, that Hadoindus, venerable bishop of the city of Le Mans, and Sigrannus, abbot of the monastery of Anille, have sent to our clemency; their envoys informed us, and confirmed the assent and petition of the aforesaid men by their letters, saying that the aforesaid abbot Sigrannus had petitioned his above-mentioned bishop Hadoindus for the aforesaid little monastery of Anille by title of precarium; in this little monastery the lord Calais also rests in the body, who himself built it and, at the dedication of the church, handed it over by instruments of charters to the lord Innocent, bishop of the aforesaid city; and the said abbot has obtained it in benefice by precarium from the above-mentioned Hadoindus. Hence their envoys also showed us the writing of the precarial letters, in which it was contained how the said abbot had requested the aforesaid little monastery from the said bishop, and had received it from him by beneficiary right for the days of his life, and, for the security of the matter, had promised to pay him a rent each year, that is, for the lighting of the mother church, 4 pounds of wax; and for the use of the brother canons serving God in the aforesaid city, on the Lord's Supper, a full measure (modius) of eggs and full flasks prepared with the best wine; and for the use of the bishop one staff and two shoes each year, which he was to pay to the side of the said bishop or of his rectors. Petitioning, therefore, they both sent letters and envoys to our highness, that, for the sake of security, we should make a precept upon the precarium of the said prelate, by which the said abbot Sigrannus might hold and possess the aforesaid little monastery safe and secure, as long as he lives, with all its entirety and appurtenances. Accordingly we have ordered this our authority to be made for the said venerable men, by which we instruct and command that the aforesaid little monastery, as it was conferred on the said abbot by beneficiary arrangement by the above-mentioned venerable bishop Hadoindus, so may henceforth remain in his beneficiary lordship, and that he take care to pay the above-written rent to the side of the rectors of the same see of Le Mans without any delay; but after his death, let it return, without anyone's detention or opposition, to the power of the said mother church of the city of Le Mans, from which he is known to have received it in benefice, so that the rectors of the same holy church may do whatever they wish to dispose concerning it by ecclesiastical right. And so that this authority may be held firmer and preserved through the ages, we have decreed to confirm it below with the subscriptions of our hand.
XXXIX.

Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which he gives to the church of Saint-Denis the church of Plumbata and many other churches, with their appurtenances, and grants it privileges (year 637).

We know it was decreed by our predecessors to the fathers that whatever was done that would profit the memory of later generations should be committed to writing, lest it be suppressed by the darkness of oblivion. Wherefore I, Dagobert, by the grace of God king of the Franks, wish it to be made known to all, future as well as present, that to the church of the blessed martyrs Denis, Rusticus and Eleutherius in Francia we give and grant, with the counsel of our magnates and the assent of the lord Ansoald, bishop of Poitiers, and of others, archbishops as well as bishops, the church of Plumbata, namely the church which the blessed confessors Ursinus, Martial, Lucian [Cacianus] and Julian built in honour of blessed Mary ever virgin and of the holy angels, and which the angels themselves consecrated to God; the church, I say, which lies between two valleys, situated near the water called the Vienne [Vigona], we grant to the aforesaid martyrs, freely absolved from service [free and absolved from all service]. Again we make known to present and future that we have given to the aforesaid martyrs vineyards, lands and meadows, with waters and woods, male and female serfs, in the same place. I do not wish it to escape you, moreover, that whoever, whether free or serf or condemned for any crime, within the bounds which I have set from the place called Aula as far as another place called Ternant, as the aforesaid water and the land of Saint Martin and of blessed Radegund show, whoever, I say, whether from a duel or a native, robber, thief, murderer, seeks refuge, shall escape free and immune from any harassment by pursuers; furthermore let it be manifest to all that those who dwell within the aforesaid place owe obedience to none but God alone and the monks of the church. We give also to the aforesaid martyrs the church of Saint Hilary within Anna [the river], with lands and tithes and waters. Likewise in the same place called Cursous [Cursona], our churches, namely the church of the holy martyrs Gervase and Protase, and another in honour of blessed Martin, and from the spring called Benedicta as far as the place called Claustrum, all the land and water called Voda, and the mill of Cumignech, and the land of Bosnay, with male and female serfs and tithes. Likewise the land of Laingniacum [Lingniacum], and the church of blessed Hilary, with lands and meadows and tithes. We have given to the holy martyrs, on the other side of the river Vienne, our village of Ingrandes [of the river Vienne, the village], with the churches namely of the apostles Peter and Paul and of the holy martyr Hippolytus, with lands and tithes, male and female serfs. Likewise on the same Vienne [Vigenna], the church of the holy apostles Peter and Paul of Dangé, with lands and tithes and serfs. Likewise our fisc of Odriacum, and the church of Saint Sulpicius, with lands and meadows and tithes and serfs, with the vicarial rights. Likewise the land of Maleredum, with meadows and vineyards and woods, male and female serfs and vicarial rights; and the other Laingniacum [Lingniacum], and the church of blessed Remigius. Likewise in the district of Tours, Antigniacum and the church of Saint Vincent on the Vienne, and the land of Selignech, with lands, tithes and serfs. Likewise in the same territory the land of Pleis, with the church of Saint Silvester, and the land of Buymet. So therefore that every false claim of adversaries may be laid to rest and fall silent, and all harassment of all malicious men may depart condemned, it has pleased us, for the sake of memory, to confirm this writing with our seal.
XL.
Diploma of Dagobert I, king of the Franks, by which, at the request of Aubert, bishop of Cambrai, he confers many gifts on the oratory of blessed Mary (year 637).

In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, amen. Since the Son of God admonishes and says: Give alms, and behold, all things are clean for you; therefore I, Dagobert, king of the Austrasians, for the soul of my dearest father Chlothar, most august king of the Franks, induced by the salutary admonitions of the venerable man and my kinsman Aubert, bishop of Cambrai, grant and give to the most pious brothers of the oratory of blessed Mary two royal fiscs, OEnengium and Karubium, with all their appurtenances, that is, slaves and bondsmen of both sexes, villas, lands, woods, meadows, waters and watercourses, etc.; likewise the villa Buriaca, the villa Haides, and in part the villas Halogin and Glevia, etc.; likewise I give and hand over to the church of Saint Peter of Cambrai, in which the most holy father Vedast established canons, the fisc Tilletum, the villas Vinciacum and Harna, with appurtenances, etc., these donations being approved by the princes and seniors of my palace, Arnulf and Pippin. And so that this our grant, etc. Sign of the lord Dagobert, king of the Austrasians. S[ign] of Arnulf of Metz. S[ign] of Pippin of Neustria, seniors of the palace. S[ign] of Anso, chancellor, in place of Cunibert, archchancellor, verified.... Given at Cambrai, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of May, in the year of the Lord six hundred and forty, indiction XIV.
